fact_statement: The nucleus of an atom is made up of positively charged protons and uncharged neutrons.

fact_statement: Modern science is commonly divided into three major branches: natural science, social science, and formal science.

fact_statement: In the Standard Model, matter particles interact via the strong, weak, and electromagnetic fundamental forces.

fact_statement: The Big Bang theory is the theory of Georges Lemaître, which was favoured over the steady-state model after the cosmic microwave background was discovered.

fact_statement: Antoine Lavoisier developed a law of conservation of mass that demanded careful measurement and quantitative observations of chemical phenomena.

fact_statement: Karl Jansky's discovery that radio signals were emitted by celestial bodies initiated the science of radio astronomy.

fact_statement: Total research funding in most developed countries is between 1.5% and 3% of GDP.

fact_statement: In the OECD, around two-thirds of research and development in scientific and technical fields is carried out by industry.

fact_statement: The movable type printing press had already produced more than 20 million volumes by the end of the 15th century.
ground_truth: It had produced more than 20 million volumes by the end of the 15th century.

fact_statement: Hydrogen and lithium need only two electrons in their outermost shell to attain a stable configuration.
ground_truth: They need only two electrons in their outermost shell.

fact_statement: Atoms that follow the octet rule combine so that each has eight electrons in its valence shell.
ground_truth: Each atom has eight electrons in its valence shell.

fact_statement: Humphry Davy discovered nine new elements, including the alkali metals, by extracting them from their oxides with electric current.
ground_truth: Humphry Davy discovered nine new elements.

fact_statement: There are three phases of solid iron (alpha, gamma, and delta) that vary based on temperature and pressure.
ground_truth: Solid iron has three phases.

fact_statement: Aristotelian physics was influential for about two millennia.
ground_truth: Aristotelian physics was influential for about two millennia.

fact_statement: Atomism was found to be correct approximately 2000 years after it was proposed by Leucippus and his pupil Democritus.
ground_truth: Atomism was found to be correct approximately 2000 years after it was proposed.

fact_statement: The structure of polyatomic molecules, which are constituted of more than six atoms, can be crucial for their chemical nature.
ground_truth: Polyatomic molecules are constituted of more than six atoms.

fact_statement: Galileo Galilei extensively cited the works of John Philoponus ten centuries later.
ground_truth: Galileo cited Philoponus's works about ten centuries later.

fact_statement: The year 2011 was chosen as the International Year of Chemistry because it was the 100th anniversary of Marie Curie's receipt of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
ground_truth: It was the 100th anniversary of Marie Curie's Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

fact_statement: The global top 50 chemical producers in 2013 had sales of US$980.5 billion.
ground_truth: They had sales of US$980.5 billion.

fact_statement: Charles Darwin's book On the Origin of Species was published in 1859.
ground_truth: On the Origin of Species was published in 1859.

fact_statement: Wilhelm Wundt founded the first laboratory for psychological research in 1879.
ground_truth: Wilhelm Wundt founded the first psychology laboratory in 1879.

fact_statement: The House of Wisdom was established in the Abbasid capital of Baghdad, Iraq.
ground_truth: The House of Wisdom was established in Baghdad, Iraq.

fact_statement: The movable type printing press spread from a single print shop in Mainz, Germany around 1440.
ground_truth: The printing press spread from a single print shop in Mainz, Germany.

fact_statement: Optics is concerned not only with visible light but also with infrared and ultraviolet radiation.
ground_truth: Optics studies visible light as well as infrared and ultraviolet radiation.

fact_statement: Social science disciplines include anthropology, economics, history, human geography, political science, psychology, and sociology.
ground_truth: Social science disciplines include anthropology, economics, history, human geography, political science, psychology, and sociology.

fact_statement: In the ionic bond of sodium chloride, sodium (a metal) loses one electron to become Na+ and chlorine (a non-metal) gains it to become Cl−.
ground_truth: Sodium loses one electron and chlorine gains it, forming Na+ and Cl−.

fact_statement: Tycho Brahe's accurate astronomical observations and Galileo Galilei's early 17th-century telescopic observations combined to turn astronomy into the first modern science.
ground_truth: Brahe's observations and Galileo's telescopic observations together turned astronomy into the first modern science.

fact_statement: A cation is a positively charged ion, while an anion is a negatively charged ion.
ground_truth: A cation is positively charged and an anion is negatively charged.

fact_statement: An electric current gives rise to a magnetic field, and a changing magnetic field induces an electric current.
ground_truth: An electric current produces a magnetic field, and a changing magnetic field induces an electric current.

fact_statement: From the 3rd millennium BCE, the ancient Egyptians developed a non-positional decimal numbering system, solved practical problems using geometry, and developed a calendar.
ground_truth: They developed a decimal numbering system, used geometry for practical problems, and developed a calendar.

fact_statement: The ancient Mesopotamians used knowledge about the properties of natural chemicals to manufacture pottery, faience, glass, soap, metals, lime plaster, and waterproofing.
ground_truth: They made pottery, faience, glass, soap, metals, lime plaster, and waterproofing.

fact_statement: Important modern branches of acoustics include ultrasonics, bioacoustics, and electroacoustics.
ground_truth: They include ultrasonics, bioacoustics, and electroacoustics.

fact_statement: Applied sciences are disciplines that use scientific knowledge for practical purposes, such as engineering and medicine.
ground_truth: Applied sciences use scientific knowledge for practical purposes, such as engineering and medicine.

fact_statement: According to Arrhenius theory, an acid produces hydronium ions when dissolved in water and a base produces hydroxide ions when dissolved in water.
ground_truth: An acid produces hydronium ions and a base produces hydroxide ions in water.

fact_statement: Quantum mechanics was pioneered by Werner Heisenberg, Erwin Schrödinger and Paul Dirac.
ground_truth: Quantum mechanics was pioneered by Heisenberg, Schrödinger and Dirac.

fact_statement: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace independently proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, which explained how different plants and animals originated and evolved.
ground_truth: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace independently proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection. The theory explained how different plants and animals originated and evolved. It was set out in detail in Darwin's book On the Origin of Species.

fact_statement: In 1897, J.J. Thomson of the University of Cambridge discovered the electron.
ground_truth: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron. He was at the University of Cambridge. The discovery was made in 1897.

fact_statement: Isaac Newton and, separately, Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz developed calculus, the mathematical study of continuous change, and Newton applied it to solve physical problems.
ground_truth: Isaac Newton and, separately, Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz developed calculus. Calculus is the mathematical study of continuous change. Newton applied it to solve physical problems.

fact_statement: In the OECD, universities carry out 20% and government carries out 10% of research and development in scientific and technical fields.
ground_truth: Universities carry out about 20% of research and development in the OECD. Government carries out about 10%. Industry carries out around two-thirds.

fact_statement: Atoms of carbon may have mass numbers of 12 or 13, and atoms of an element with different mass numbers are known as isotopes.
ground_truth: Carbon atoms may have mass numbers of 12 or 13. Atoms of an element with different mass numbers are called isotopes.

fact_statement: Chemistry is illustrated through six main branches: inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, physical chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, and applied chemistry.
ground_truth: There are six main branches of chemistry. They are inorganic, organic, physical, and analytical chemistry, plus biochemistry and applied chemistry.

fact_statement: When three states of matter meet based on the conditions, it is known as a triple point, which is invariant and so a convenient way to define a set of conditions.
ground_truth: A triple point occurs when three states meet. It is invariant. This makes it a convenient way to define a set of conditions.

fact_statement: The noble gas elements are helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon, and they are composed of lone atoms as their smallest discrete unit.
ground_truth: There are six noble gases: helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon. Their smallest discrete unit is a lone atom.

fact_statement: Boyle's law dates to 1662, Charles's law to 1787, Dalton's law to 1803, and Gay-Lussac's law to 1809.
ground_truth: Boyle's law dates to 1662. Charles's law dates to 1787. Dalton's law dates to 1803. Gay-Lussac's law dates to 1809.

fact_statement: Ernest Rutherford carried out his pioneering scattering experiments at the University of Manchester, discovering the internal structure of the atom and the existence of the proton.
ground_truth: Rutherford worked at the University of Manchester. There he discovered the internal structure of the atom. He also discovered the existence of the proton.

fact_statement: The Milesian school was founded by Thales of Miletus and continued by Anaximander and Anaximenes, who were the first to attempt to explain natural phenomena without relying on the supernatural.
ground_truth: Thales of Miletus founded the Milesian school. Anaximander and Anaximenes continued it. They were the first to try to explain natural phenomena without the supernatural.

fact_statement: The scientific method is an empirical cycle that typically involves making observations, producing hypotheses, testing them with evidence, and drawing conclusions.
ground_truth: The scientific method is an empirical cycle. It involves making observations and producing hypotheses. It also involves testing them with evidence and drawing conclusions.

fact_statement: A theory typically describes the behaviour of much broader sets of observations than a hypothesis, and a large number of hypotheses can be logically bound together by a single theory.
ground_truth: A theory describes much broader sets of observations than a hypothesis. Many hypotheses can be logically bound together by a single theory. Thus a theory is a hypothesis explaining various other hypotheses.

fact_statement: In redox reactions, atoms change oxidation state by gaining electrons (reduction) or losing electrons (oxidation).
ground_truth: Redox reactions change atoms' oxidation states. Gaining electrons is reduction and losing electrons is oxidation. An oxidant removes electrons from another substance, while a reductant transfers electrons and is itself oxidized.

fact_statement: Aristotle's successor Theophrastus began the scientific study of plants.
ground_truth: Theophrastus

fact_statement: Biology began to develop quickly with Anton van Leeuwenhoek's dramatic improvement of the microscope.
ground_truth: Anton van Leeuwenhoek

fact_statement: Serious evolutionary thinking originated with the works of Jean-Baptiste Lamarck, who presented a coherent theory of evolution.
ground_truth: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck

fact_statement: The geographer Eratosthenes accurately calculated the circumference of the Earth.
ground_truth: Eratosthenes

fact_statement: Aristotle classified more than 540 animal species.
ground_truth: More than 540

fact_statement: Aristotle dissected at least 50 of the animal species he studied.
ground_truth: At least 50

fact_statement: The Mohenjo-daro ruler, approximately 34 mm long, was divided into ten equal parts.
ground_truth: Ten

fact_statement: The official Egyptian calendar had twelve months of thirty days each plus five days at the end of the year.
ground_truth: Five

fact_statement: The Maya developed a positional numeral system with a base of 20 that included the use of zero.
Pāṇini's grammar formulates close to 4,000 rules for Sanskrit.
ground_truth: Close to 4,000

fact_statement: Chinese astronomical observations include 112 sunspot records from 364 BCE.
Zu Chongzhi's ratio for pi remained the most accurate value for 1200 years.
ground_truth: 1200 years

fact_statement: Carl Linnaeus published a basic taxonomy for the natural world in 1735.
Aristotle observed the habits and attributes of plants and animals on Lesbos.
ground_truth: Lesbos

fact_statement: Ecology is the study of the distribution and abundance of life and the interaction between organisms and their environment.
ground_truth: Distribution and abundance of life

fact_statement: Robert Remak and Rudolf Virchow reified the third tenet of cell theory.
ground_truth: Remak and Virchow

fact_statement: The genetic code was cracked by Har Gobind Khorana, Robert W. Holley and Marshall Warren Nirenberg.
ground_truth: Khorana, Holley, and Nirenberg

fact_statement: A series of experiments by Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase pointed to DNA as the component of chromosomes that held genes.
ground_truth: Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase

fact_statement: The Trivium of medieval university studies consisted of grammar, rhetoric, and logic.
ground_truth: Grammar, rhetoric, and logic

fact_statement: The Quadrivium consisted of arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, and music.
ground_truth: Arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, and music

fact_statement: Aristotle believed that everything was derived from the elements earth, water, air, fire, and Aether.
ground_truth: Earth, water, air, fire, Aether

fact_statement: Euclid introduced the concepts of definition, axiom, theorem and proof in his Elements.
ground_truth: Definition, axiom, theorem, and proof

fact_statement: Jan Swammerdam's investigations led to new interest in entomology and helped develop techniques of microscopic dissection and staining.
ground_truth: Jan Swammerdam's investigations led to new interest in entomology.

fact_statement: Georges-Louis Leclerc, Comte de Buffon, treated species as artificial categories and living forms as malleable, even suggesting the possibility of common descent.
ground_truth: Georges-Louis Leclerc, Comte de Buffon, did.

fact_statement: Theodosius Dobzhansky famously said that nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution.
ground_truth: Theodosius Dobzhansky said it.

fact_statement: Thomas Hunt Morgan's experiments with fruit flies supported the chromosome theory of inheritance by establishing sex linkage between eye color and sex.
ground_truth: Thomas Hunt Morgan's experiments did.

fact_statement: Herophilos was the first to base his conclusions on dissection of the human body and to describe the nervous system.
ground_truth: Herophilos was the first.

fact_statement: Pliny the Elder was the first to show that amber was a resin from pine trees, because of the insects trapped within it.
ground_truth: Pliny the Elder was the first.

fact_statement: Shen Kuo was the first to describe the magnetic-needle compass used for navigation.
ground_truth: Shen Kuo was the first to describe it.

fact_statement: The Indus Valley Civilisation made bricks whose dimensions were in the proportion 4:2:1.
ground_truth: Their dimensions were in the proportion 4:2:1.

fact_statement: An earthquake indicated by Zhang Heng's seismometer was confirmed to have struck 400 to 500 km northwest of Luoyang.
ground_truth: It struck 400 to 500 km northwest of Luoyang.

fact_statement: The domestication of maize for agriculture has been dated to about 9,000 years ago in southern Mexico.
ground_truth: It has been dated to about 9,000 years ago.

fact_statement: The Rigveda describes a year of 360 days divided into 12 equal parts of 30 days each.
ground_truth: The year has 360 days.

fact_statement: Liu Hui calculated pi to 5 significant figures in the 3rd century CE.
ground_truth: Liu Hui calculated pi to 5 significant figures.

fact_statement: Marcus Terentius Varro wrote the encyclopedia Nine Books of Disciplines, which covered nine arts.
ground_truth: It covered nine arts.

fact_statement: Jai Singh II of Jaipur constructed five observatories called Jantar Mantars in total.
ground_truth: He constructed five.

fact_statement: Galen performed audacious operations, including brain and eye surgeries, that were not tried again for almost two millennia.
ground_truth: They were not tried again for almost two millennia.

fact_statement: The Mesopotamian cuneiform tablet Plimpton 322 records a number of Pythagorean triplets, including (3, 4, 5) and (5, 12, 13).
ground_truth: It records (3, 4, 5) and (5, 12, 13).

fact_statement: The 3-4-5 right triangle and other rules of geometry were used in ancient Egypt to build rectilinear structures.
ground_truth: The 3-4-5 right triangle.

fact_statement: Scientific thinking emerged gradually over the course of tens of thousands of years.
ground_truth: It emerged over tens of thousands of years.

fact_statement: Copernicus' model never displaced Ptolemy's, which only fell out of favor 70 years later after Galileo's telescopic observations of 1610.
ground_truth: It fell out of favor 70 years later.

fact_statement: During the 3rd and 4th centuries CE, the Roman Empire was administratively divided into two halves: the Greek East and the Latin West.
ground_truth: It was divided into two halves.

fact_statement: Daniel Bernoulli conceived gases as numerous particles in rapid random motion in Hydrodynamica (1738).
ground_truth: Hydrodynamica is dated 1738.

fact_statement: In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick discovered the double-helical structure of DNA.
ground_truth: They discovered it in 1953.

fact_statement: Su Song erected a large astronomical clocktower in Kaifeng city in 1088.
ground_truth: In Kaifeng city.

fact_statement: Megalithic structures at Nabta Playa, Upper Egypt, featured astronomy and calendar arrangements aligned with the heliacal rising of Sirius.
ground_truth: At Nabta Playa in Upper Egypt.

fact_statement: Subdisciplines of biology include molecular biology, physiology, ecology, evolutionary biology, developmental biology, and systematics.
ground_truth: They include molecular biology, physiology, ecology, evolutionary biology, developmental biology, and systematics.

fact_statement: Biology examines life across multiple levels of organization, from molecules and cells to organisms, populations, and ecosystems.
ground_truth: From molecules and cells to organisms, populations, and ecosystems.

fact_statement: Biologists classify organisms from single-celled archaea and bacteria to multicellular plants, fungi, and animals.
ground_truth: They classify single-celled archaea and bacteria and multicellular plants, fungi, and animals.

fact_statement: Molecular biology examines how macromolecules orchestrate processes such as replication, transcription, translation, protein synthesis, and complex biomolecular interactions.
ground_truth: Replication, transcription, translation, protein synthesis, and complex biomolecular interactions.

fact_statement: The Ebers and Edwin Smith papyri applied examination, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis to the treatment of disease.
ground_truth: Examination, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis.

fact_statement: Students in the lower faculty of medieval universities who worked towards a Magister degree studied three philosophies: metaphysics, ethics, and natural philosophy.
ground_truth: They studied metaphysics, ethics, and natural philosophy.

fact_statement: In East Semitic cultures the main medicinal authority was an exorcist-healer called an asipu, while a less frequent healer called an asu corresponded more closely to a modern physician.
ground_truth: The main authority was the asipu, an exorcist-healer, and the less frequent healer was the asu, closer to a modern physician.

fact_statement: Thales postulated that land floats on water and that earthquakes are caused by the agitation of that water, rather than by the god Poseidon.
ground_truth: Land floats on water, and earthquakes are caused by the agitation of that water.

fact_statement: Physics deals with the structure of matter and the interactions between the fundamental constituents of the observable universe, including the behavior of objects under forces and gravitational, electromagnetic, and nuclear force fields.
ground_truth: Physics deals with the structure of matter and the interactions between the fundamental constituents of the observable universe, including forces and gravitational, electromagnetic, and nuclear force fields.

fact_statement: Chemistry is the science of the properties, composition, and structure of substances (defined as elements and compounds), the transformations they undergo, and the energy that is released or absorbed during these processes.
ground_truth: Chemistry is the science of the properties, composition, and structure of elements and compounds, their transformations, and the energy released or absorbed.

fact_statement: Astronomical periods identified by Mesopotamian proto-scientists, such as the solar year and the lunar month, are still widely used in Western calendars.
ground_truth: The solar year and the lunar month.

fact_statement: The chemical bond can be a covalent bond, an ionic bond, a hydrogen bond or just because of Van der Waals force.
ground_truth: It can be a covalent bond, an ionic bond, a hydrogen bond, or due to Van der Waals force.

fact_statement: In 1838, Schleiden and Schwann began promoting the ideas that the basic unit of organisms is the cell and that individual cells have all the characteristics of life.
ground_truth: Schleiden and Schwann began promoting these ideas. They held that the basic unit of organisms is the cell. They also held that individual cells have all the characteristics of life.

fact_statement: Medical teachers and students at Bologna began to open human bodies, and Mondino de Luzzi produced the first known anatomy textbook based on human dissection.
ground_truth: Mondino de Luzzi produced the first known anatomy textbook based on human dissection. Medical teachers and students at Bologna had begun to open human bodies. Dissection had usually been banned in classical antiquity.

fact_statement: Ibn Sina (Avicenna) wrote the Kitab al-shifa (Book of Healing) and The Canon of Medicine, both used as standard medicinal texts in the Muslim world and Europe well into the 17th century.
ground_truth: Ibn Sina, known as Avicenna in the West, wrote two notable medical works. They were the Book of Healing and The Canon of Medicine. Both were used as standard medicinal texts in the Muslim world and Europe well into the 17th century.

fact_statement: Central to biology are five fundamental themes: the cell as the basic unit of life, genes and heredity, evolution, energy transformation, and homeostasis.
ground_truth: There are five themes. They are the cell as the basic unit of life, and genes and heredity as the basis of inheritance. They also include evolution as the driver of biological diversity, energy transformation for sustaining life processes, and homeostasis.

fact_statement: By the 1860s most biologists accepted all three tenets of cell theory: the cell is the basic unit of organisms, individual cells have all the characteristics of life, and all cells come from the division of other cells.
ground_truth: There were three tenets. The cell is the basic unit of organisms. Individual cells have all the characteristics of life, and all cells come from the division of other cells.

fact_statement: In the Middle Ages, classical learning continued in three major linguistic cultures and civilizations: Greek, Arabic, and Latin.
ground_truth: There were three. They were Greek (the Byzantine Empire), Arabic (the Islamic world), and Latin (Western Europe).

fact_statement: The Siddhanta Shiromani, written by Bhaskara in the 12th century, has a second part of 13 chapters covering the nature of the sphere and significant astronomical and trigonometric calculations based on it.
ground_truth: The second part has 13 chapters. They cover the nature of the sphere. They also cover significant astronomical and trigonometric calculations based on it.

fact_statement: The first seven of Varro's nine arts would later define the seven liberal arts of medieval schools.
ground_truth: Seven. It was the first seven of Varro's nine arts that later defined the seven liberal arts of medieval schools.

fact_statement: The term biology in its modern sense appears to have been introduced independently by Thomas Beddoes (1799), Karl Friedrich Burdach (1800), Gottfried Reinhold Treviranus (1802) and Jean-Baptiste Lamarck (1802).
ground_truth: Thomas Beddoes introduced it in 1799. Karl Friedrich Burdach introduced it in 1800. Gottfried Reinhold Treviranus and Jean-Baptiste Lamarck introduced it in 1802.

fact_statement: The metallurgical achievements of the Cistercian blast furnace at Laskill are cited among the technological advances of the Middle Ages.
ground_truth: The furnace was at Laskill. It was a Cistercian blast furnace. It is cited for its metallurgical achievements among medieval technological advances.

fact_statement: Evolutionary developmental biology explores deep homology, the finding that dissimilar organs such as the eyes of insects, vertebrates and cephalopod molluscs, long thought to have evolved separately, are controlled by similar genes from the evo-devo gene toolkit.
ground_truth: Deep homology is the finding that dissimilar organs, long thought to have evolved separately, are controlled by similar genes. Examples are the eyes of insects, vertebrates and cephalopod molluscs. The genes come from the evo-devo gene toolkit.

fact_statement: Conservation biology studies the conservation of Earth's biodiversity with the aim of protecting species, their habitats, and ecosystems from excessive rates of extinction and the erosion of biotic interactions.
ground_truth: Conservation biology is the study of the conservation of Earth's biodiversity. Its aim is to protect species, their habitats, and ecosystems. It protects them from excessive rates of extinction and the erosion of biotic interactions.

fact_statement: At a madrasa, students learned from one specific teacher, who issued a certificate called an Ijazah, which is a license to teach and pass on a very specific set of texts.
ground_truth: Madrasa students learned from one specific teacher. The teacher issued a certificate called an Ijazah. It was a license to teach and pass on a very specific set of texts.

fact_statement: The legacy of the classical Greek period included substantial advances in factual knowledge, especially in anatomy, zoology, botany, mineralogy, geography, mathematics and astronomy.
ground_truth: The legacy included substantial advances in factual knowledge. These were especially in anatomy, zoology, botany, mineralogy, geography, mathematics and astronomy.

fact_statement: Al-Battani improved the measurements of Hipparchus preserved in Ptolemy's Almagest.
ground_truth: Al-Battani

fact_statement: The discovery of the pulmonary transit of blood in the human body by Ibn al-Nafis occurred in a hospital setting.
ground_truth: Ibn al-Nafis

fact_statement: The first 12 chapters of the Siddhanta Shiromani cover topics such as mean longitudes of the planets, true longitudes of the planets, and lunar and solar eclipses.
ground_truth: The first 12

fact_statement: Maya writing contains calendar dates for tracking social, religious, political, and economic events in 360-day years.
ground_truth: 360 days

fact_statement: Earth, water, air, and fire were each derived from a combination of two of the characteristics hot, wet, cold, and dry.
ground_truth: Two

fact_statement: The Mesopotamian tablet Plimpton 322 hints that the ancient Mesopotamians might have been aware of the Pythagorean theorem over a millennium before Pythagoras.
ground_truth: Over a millennium

fact_statement: Narayana Pandita wrote the Ganita Kaumudi in 1356.
Hulagu Khan, who led the siege of Baghdad, became a patron of the Maragheh observatory.
ground_truth: Maragheh

fact_statement: The Scientific Revolution is frequently said to have begun in 1543 with the printings of De humani corporis fabrica by Andreas Vesalius and De Revolutionibus by Nicolaus Copernicus.
ground_truth: Vesalius and Copernicus

fact_statement: Charles Darwin combined the biogeographical approach of Humboldt, the uniformitarian geology of Lyell, and Malthus's writings on population growth with his own observations to forge a more successful evolutionary theory.
ground_truth: Humboldt, Lyell, and Malthus

fact_statement: Students who completed the baccalaureate at medieval universities could join the higher faculty of law, medicine, or theology.
ground_truth: Law, medicine, and theology

fact_statement: Nilakantha Somayaji updated the Aryabhatan model for the interior planets Mercury and Venus in the Tantrasangraha.
ground_truth: Nilakantha Somayaji updated the Aryabhatan model for Mercury and Venus.

fact_statement: Madhava of Sangamagrama led advancement in analysis by providing the infinite and Taylor series expansion of some trigonometric functions and a pi approximation.
ground_truth: Madhava of Sangamagrama provided them.

fact_statement: John Philoponus, a Byzantine scholar, was the first to question Aristotle's teaching of physics, introducing the theory of impetus.
ground_truth: John Philoponus was the first.

fact_statement: Jean Buridan developed the theory that impetus was the cause of the motion of projectiles.
ground_truth: Jean Buridan developed it.

fact_statement: Indian logic stands as one of the three original traditions of logic, alongside the Greek and the Chinese logic.
ground_truth: Indian logic is one of three original traditions of logic.

fact_statement: The eastward transmission of Greek heritage to Western Asia was a slow and gradual process that spanned over a thousand years.
ground_truth: It spanned over a thousand years.

fact_statement: Maya logographs represent calendar periods amounting to 20 days and even 20 years.
ground_truth: The periods amount to 20 days and even 20 years.

fact_statement: The compound biologia appears in the title of Volume 3 of Michael Christoph Hanow's Philosophiae naturalis sive physicae dogmaticae.
ground_truth: It appears in the title of Volume 3.

fact_statement: The Catuskoti is also often glossed Tetralemma, the name for a largely comparable but not equatable four corner argument within classical logic.
ground_truth: It is described as a four corner argument.

fact_statement: Records of the motions of the stars, planets, and the moon in Babylonian astronomy are left on thousands of clay tablets created by scribes.
ground_truth: They are left on thousands of clay tablets.

fact_statement: William Harvey published De Motu Cordis in 1628.
ground_truth: He published it in 1628.

fact_statement: The Zapotec civilization established the first known full writing system of the Pre-Columbian region of Mesoamerica.
ground_truth: In Mesoamerica.

fact_statement: The oral tradition of preliterate societies was fluid, tended to describe the universe as just sky and earth with a potential underworld, and identified causes with beginnings.
ground_truth: It was fluid, described the universe as sky and earth with a potential underworld, and identified causes with beginnings.

fact_statement: Evolutionary research fields that try to explain phenomena poorly accounted for in the modern evolutionary synthesis include speciation, the evolution of sexual reproduction, the evolution of cooperation, the evolution of ageing, and evolvability.
ground_truth: They include speciation, the evolution of sexual reproduction, cooperation, ageing, and evolvability.

fact_statement: Classical genetics studies how genes and traits are passed on from parents to offspring, and its principles are called Mendelian inheritance.
ground_truth: It studies how genes and traits pass from parents to offspring, and its principles are called Mendelian inheritance.

fact_statement: Bioenergetics is a field in biochemistry and cell biology concerned with energy flow through living systems, including cellular respiration and other metabolic and enzymatic processes.
ground_truth: It concerns energy flow through living systems, including cellular respiration and metabolic and enzymatic processes.

fact_statement: The Susrutasamhita of Susruta describes surgical procedures including rhinoplasty, repair of torn ear lobes, perineal lithotomy, and cataract surgery.
ground_truth: It describes rhinoplasty, repair of torn ear lobes, perineal lithotomy, and cataract surgery.

fact_statement: Islamic trigonometry continued from Ptolemy's Almagest and the Indian Siddhanta, added trigonometric functions and tables, and applied trigonometry to spheres and planes.
ground_truth: It added trigonometric functions, drew up tables, and applied trigonometry to spheres and planes.

fact_statement: Brahmagupta suggested in 628 that gravity was a force of attraction and lucidly explained zero as both a placeholder and a decimal digit, along with the Hindu-Arabic numeral system.
ground_truth: Brahmagupta suggested in 628 that gravity was a force of attraction.He lucidly explained the use of zero as both a placeholder and a decimal digit.He also explained the Hindu-Arabic numeral system now used universally.

fact_statement: Navya-Nyaya systematised all Nyaya concepts into four main categories: perception, inference, comparison, and testimony.
ground_truth: Navya-Nyaya systematised all Nyaya concepts into four main categories.The first is sense or perception (pratyaksa).The second is inference (anumana).The third is comparison or similarity (upamana).The fourth is testimony (sound or word; sabda).

fact_statement: The Bakhshali manuscript covers fractions, square roots, progressions, simple and simultaneous linear equations, quadratic equations, and indeterminate equations of the second degree.
ground_truth: The Bakhshali manuscript contains problems involving arithmetic, algebra and geometry, including mensuration.Its topics include fractions, square roots, and arithmetic and geometric progressions.It covers solutions of simple equations and simultaneous linear equations.It also includes quadratic equations and indeterminate equations of the second degree.

fact_statement: In their natural state, earth is closest to the Earth, followed by water, air, fire, and finally Aether, with Aether making up the celestial bodies.
ground_truth: In their natural state, earth is closest to the Earth, followed by water, air, fire, and finally Aether.Water sits above earth, air above water, and fire above air.Aether was a celestial element and made up the matter of the celestial bodies.

fact_statement: Ibn al-Haytham synthesized a new theory of vision including a complete system of geometrical optics, set out in his Book of Optics, which was translated into Latin and relied upon in Europe until the 17th century.
ground_truth: Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) synthesized a new theory of vision in the 11th century, based on the works of his predecessors.His theory included a complete system of geometrical optics.It was set out in great detail in his Book of Optics.The book was translated into Latin.It was relied upon as a principal source on optics in Europe until the 17th century.

fact_statement: According to Joseph Needham, Chinese technological accomplishments included the water-powered celestial globe, dry docks, sliding calipers, the double-action piston pump, the blast furnace, the multi-tube seed drill, the wheelbarrow, the suspension bridge, the winnowing machine, gunpowder, the raised-relief map, toilet paper, and the efficient harness.
ground_truth: According to Joseph Needham, accomplishments included the water-powered celestial globe (Zhang Heng), dry docks, and sliding calipers.They also included the double-action piston pump, the blast furnace, and the multi-tube seed drill.Further examples were the wheelbarrow, the suspension bridge, and the winnowing machine.They also included gunpowder, the raised-relief map, toilet paper, and the efficient harness.

fact_statement: Nubian bone remains between 350 AD and 550 AD show tetracycline use, which was in wide commercial use only in the mid 20th century, possibly from Streptomyces in grain jars used for making beer.
ground_truth: Nubian mummies studied in the 1990s revealed that Kush was a pioneer of early antibiotics.Tetracycline was being used by Nubians, based on bone remains between 350 AD and 550 AD.The antibiotic was in wide commercial use only in the mid 20th century.The theory is that earthen jars containing grain for making beer contained the bacterium Streptomyces, which produced tetracycline.Nubians were not aware of tetracycline.
